items.note: Association named, organized 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose first president, creamery built 1891 - all present in story 1.
Article VII given as pay by the station's own butterfat test, not the weight of milk delivered - both required elements present in story 1.
Section A never states that the rule is what made a wrong test cost money. The equivalent claim appears only at B3; credit does not travel from B-G into A.
Effie Loomis and Wilbur Teague absent from Section A. Only Hobart Sill appears, incidentally as a recollection source; one of three officers is not the item.
Selby Vose is never mentioned inside Section A. He appears only at B3/B4, and there with the wrong start year (1911).
The station-gain ledger line appears only at C1(a). Nothing about it inside Section A.
Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles up the valley, opened 4 May 1896, glassware borrowed from Larrow Green (Sill's outfit) - all in story 1.
No description anywhere in Section A of how testing worked: no weighing at intake, no composite sample, no percent on the graduated neck, no fixed charge.

Ammon & Sons named, invoice of 14 April 1897 given, entry into service dated spring 1897 with Orra Keddie's 1 May 1897 diary entry; 1898/1899 correctly rejected as outliers. Tarnet not named, but the core fact is stated.

The invoice line items are listed but the two gated figures are missing: no 6 dozen pipettes and no 17.6 c.c. marking. The total is left as an unresolved $77.93/$77.39 gap (and $77.39 is asserted as better-attested in the method note - see deductions).
The flat, every-month 0.19 shortfall as the signature of an instrument is never stated in Section A; the 0.19 figure appears only at C1(b).
No mention of a pipette being uncheckable without a burette, or of there being none in the county.
Ansel Keddie, tester and separator man at Ostrey Hollow from the 1896 opening, 29 seasons, ending 1925. Service and its end - A3.1's own aspect - is stated.

The test book is named as Keddie's own record, kept in his hand (the 1911 note and question mark written into it). Bold gate is 'test book'; the column list and the crossed-and-initialed corrections are unbolded context.
The summary leaf's two figures (3.80 for 1896, 3.61 from 1898) appear nowhere in Section A - story 3 says only that tests 'rose markedly'. 3.61/3.80 are given at C1(b), which cannot carry an A item.

Nine weeks of 1911, break on 8 May, borrowed measure to 10 July, readings up through the interval and back down the day the station's own glass returned, and Keddie's question mark. Only the 3.80 figure is missing; core fact intact.
Section A gives Orra Keddie as the tester's wife but never that she was Orra Brant, sister of Emmet Brant. The sibling link is stated only at B1/B2.
The 1919 circular is not in Section A (only 'the 1919 revival'); it appears at B3/B4. Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement is absent entirely.
Keddie's death in 1934 and the fate of the test book are not in Section A. The only 1934 reference is Sill's recollection.

Answer 'granddaughter' correct (1). Derivation credited (1): Falke's named, dated post-type self-correction - one of the two resolutions the key expects - plus the Orra-Brant/Duncan chain establishing Duncan as Ansel's son. The final link (Ivy as Duncan's daughter) is explicitly left unproven, which is weaker than the key's derivation but still a documented derivation.

Second cousins with the full derivation (Orra/Emmet siblings, Roy/Duncan first cousins, Hazel and Ivy their children): 1 point. Abstention item A08 not earned: the answer never raises whether Emmet and Orra were full or half siblings, so it neither declines it nor asserts it - 0, and no gullibility deduction.

Gideon Vose named as father with three independent sources against the nephew story (1). Significance correct (1): Gideon wrote Article VII making the station's own test decide pay, and his son as manager signed the 1919 circular accusing the patrons - the accuser enforcing his father's rule.

Abstention pole A01 credited (1): the answer refuses to convert the loose thread into a kinship claim, says a closer tie may exist that the sources do not name, and flags rather than resolves - leaning negative while declining is a correct abstention, so no -2. Second point lost: 'what is established' is answered with the institutional employer/tester relationship and the false claim that nothing in the sources states or implies a connection; the key's establisheds (two narrators asserting cousinship from talk, one flat denial, no document either way, a family denial not being a record) are absent.

Answer 5.25%/5.26%. Key requires 16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95, i.e. 95 percent of true, short 5 percent. The run also fails the second half of the question - it derives the figure from the ledger and from 0.19/3.61, never from the glassware.
True average 3.80, recorded short by 0.19 point. Exact match.
40,000,000 x 0.0019 = 76,000 lb. Exact match, with a correct cross-check. The 67,000 lb figure is attributed to the patrons' 1925 estimate rather than adopted, so no deduction.
Gives $19,600 and 19.4 percent. Key requires $19,000 and 20 percent / one fifth; $19,600 is a planted value (NT-8) and is asserted here as 'the best-attested total' - see deductions.
Declines. Not an abstention item: the key's answer is 200,000 x 3.42% = 6,840 lb.
Declines. Key: true test 3.42/0.95 = 3.60, true fat 7,200 lb, owed 360 lb.
Declines. Key: 360 x $0.24 = $86.40 (or $90.00 only with an explicit stated use of the 25c period average). No abstention credit exists for this item.

deductions.reason: Selby Vose asserted as manager from 1911 (B3 and B4). Planted error X94; correct year is 1913.
The patrons' loss asserted as $19,600 at C1(d) - 'the best-attested total'. Planted error X41/X74 (NT-8); correct figure is $19,000.
Method note asserts the 1897 invoice total $77.39 is 'the better-attested figure, with $77.93 the outlier'. Planted error X75/X81 (NT-14); correct total is $77.93.
Method note asserts 1922 is the date of the glassware's condemnation. Planted error X96; the condemnation was 12 June 1923.
